title: Legacy Function Lexicon and Compatibility Resolver
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Customers and internal runtime integrations use two overlapping invocation paradigms: OpenAI-style 'tools' and Redwood legacy 'functions'. Names collide, signatures differ, and customers migrating from legacy SDKs experience brittle failures. This ticket creates a canonical runtime lexicon and a deterministic resolution service that normalizes names, chooses the right target (tool vs legacy function), and exposes tolerant fallback semantics for mismatches.

Goals:
- Provide a deterministic name-resolution chain with observable decisions.
- Offer runtime-side remapping (manifest-driven) + heuristic fallbacks for ad-hoc requests.
- Ensure structured-output and streaming call paths remain compatible when a call is remapped.
- Ship a small migration utility to backfill historical call records and to generate a recommended alias manifest.

Non-goals:
- Replace existing bridge shims at the application layer. This is a platform-level resolver, not a language SDK rewrite.

Constraints:
- Must not increase p95 invocation latency by more than 2ms for cold resolutions.
- All changes must be observable in console and exportable to logs and billing pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a /resolve endpoint that returns a canonical name, resolution path, and confidence label for an invocation
Resolver uses manifest alias if present, otherwise deterministic heuristics (normalized name, tokenized similarity, namespace prefix), then falls back to legacy function names
Console shows resolution metrics: resolution_latency_ms, ambiguity_count, remapped_invocations, fallback_rate
Streaming + structured output flows remain intact when a call is remapped; end-to-end integration test demonstrates tool_stream -> resolved_function_stream with no token loss
Migration utility generates alias suggestions for 90% of historical calls in a sample customer bucket and outputs a manifest compatible with runtime manifest schema
Documentation and runbook published with examples and a recommended rollout checklist
design_notes: Canonical lexicon is a small JSON manifest: list of canonical_name -> [aliases], signature_hash, preferred_schema_version
Name normalization: lowercasing, strip punctuation, collapse underscores and dashes, remove common prefixes (e.g., 'fn_', 'tool_')
Matching precedence: explicit manifest alias > explicit metadata 'tool_name' in request > exact name match > normalized name match > fuzzy token overlap (threshold 0.7) > legacy fallback

Signature compatibility: runtime computes a lightweight signature hash from parameter names+types; prefer exact signature match; if name match but signature mismatch, use tolerant adapter that maps missing/extra params into a structured 'params' blob and logs a compatibility event
Streaming considerations: resolver must return resolution before stream head is emitted. For pre-resolved long-lived streams we cache resolution with TTL=5m and a hot-reload hook for manifest updates
Backpressure/latency trade-offs: prefer non-blocking cache lookup with background manifest refresh; on cache miss resolve synchronously but record resolution_latency for observability
Telemetry schema: event 'resolve_attempt' includes request_name, resolved_name, path_taken, confidence, resolution_latency_ms, signature_match (exact|tolerant|none), and migration_hint
Security: resolver does not change authorization checks; RBAC evaluation runs after resolution using the resolved entity name
implementation_plan: Spike (done): prototype in runtime/lexicon-service branch to validate resolution API and signature hash approach
Server: add lexicon service with in-memory cache and manifest hot-reload; implement /resolve HTTP API and internal SDK binding
Runtime integration: call resolver in the pre-invoke pipeline; implement tolerant adapter for signature mismatches
Migration utility: CLI that scans call logs, computes likely aliases, and emits manifest suggestions
Console: add dashboard widgets for resolution metrics and a manifest editor with change history
E2E tests: streaming-preservation tests + structured output roundtrip for remapped calls
Docs: runtime docs, migration guide, rollbacks and runbook
rollout_plan: Canary run in staging with synthetic workloads that exercise name collisions
Pilot with 3 internal teams (SDK gateway, Console exports, and Dedicated customers) for 2 weeks
Collect metrics, iterate on fuzzy threshold and signature rules
Gradual rollout to hosted API with opt-in manifest flag enabled by default for new accounts
Offer migration assistance and manifest generation for existing large customers via Solutions SE
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positive remaps could route calls to wrong handlers. Mitigation: require explicit manifest alias for high-risk mappings and log ambiguity with a 'dry-run' mode before enforcement
Risk: Increased p95 due to synchronous resolution on cold path. Mitigation: aggressively cache common mappings and pre-warm cache during deployment
Risk: Signature adapter may mask real contract breakages. Mitigation: emit compatibility alerts and surface them in console with recommended action
Risk: Migration CLI suggestions might create noisy manifests. Mitigation: include confidence score and require user approval before applying
